sentences.text: Guemesia ochoai is the only known species in its genus and stands as one of the smallest abelisaurid dinosaurs known to science.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a small, nearly complete braincase.
Its skull roof is highly ornamented, a feature similar to other members of this dinosaur group.
The genus name honors the military leader Martín Miguel de Güemes, while the species name honors technician Javier Ochoa.
The fossil was discovered in the Amblayo Valley within the Los Blanquitos Formation of Salta Province, Argentina.
The species was formally described in 2022 by the research team led by Agnolín.
The same formation containing Guemesia fossils also yields remains of the theropod Unquillosaurus and potential titanosaurs.
Taxonomically, Guemesia is classified as a derived abelisaurid belonging to the clade Brachyrostra.

Guemesia lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Campanian stage, approximately 84 to 71 million years ago, with the fossil record spanning from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
